instruction: I want to increase VLC's maximum volume limit beyond the default 125%. How do I configure VLC to allow a maximum volume of 200% for better audio amplification?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to configure VLC's maximum volume to 200% (qt-max-volume=200). The evaluator checks the vlcrc config file for the 'qt-max-volume' setting and verifies it is set to 200. Using existing metric function check_qt_max_volume from vlc.py. Default value is 125.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_qt_max_volume metric which checks the qt-max-volume setting in VLC config file (default is 125, task requires setting to 200)

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: get_vlc_config extracts the VLC configuration file from the appropriate OS-specific path (Linux: ~/.config/vlc/vlcrc, macOS: ~/Library/Preferences/org.videolan.vlc/vlcrc, Windows: ~\AppData\Roaming\vlc\vlcrc)
Metric logic is correct: check_qt_max_volume reads the config file, searches for 'qt-max-volume=' setting, extracts the value, and compares it to the expected value of 200
Expected value is correct: The instruction requires setting VLC max volume to 200%, and the evaluator expects 'expected_qt_max_volume: 200'
Complete coverage: The instruction has one requirement (configure max volume to 200%), and the evaluator checks exactly that requirement
Appropriate postconfig: Kills and relaunches VLC to ensure the config file is reloaded and the setting was persisted to disk
Adequate edge case handling: Metric handles missing config file (returns 0), missing setting (defaults to '125'), and type conversion for expected values
